name: Illinois
subtitle: Independent subnational IML profile. Illinois combines broad Medicaid and public-health exchange infrastructure with fragmented statewide HIE governance and material, repeatedly documented cybersecurity and control weaknesses. Federal United States scores are not inherited.
strengths: HealthChoice Illinois ADT provides a statewide Medicaid data-exchange platform using HL7 admission, discharge and transfer notifications, with all managed care organizations onboarded and multiple provider classes required to participate.
Illinois public-health surveillance has broad hospital connectivity: IDPH reports syndromic data from all 185 acute-care hospitals, with most facilities sending near-real-time data.
Illinois maintains explicit HIE privacy and opt-out protections, and provider access systems use NPI-based enrollment and individual identity proofing.
Statewide EVV aggregation and recurring ADT collaboration groups show continuing investment in operational data exchange rather than a purely policy-level framework.
watch: Illinois no longer operates the former state-run ILHIE model. The Illinois Health Information Exchange and Technology Act was repealed in 2023 and the former HIE Office was dissolved; current exchange is distributed across HFS, IDPH, federal requirements and vendor-mediated networks.

The 2022 State Medicaid Health Information Technology Plan described the former state-run HIE as financially unsustainable and noted limited commitment to regional HIE options, with providers relying substantially on vendor-mediated networks. This source is historical context and is not treated as proof of the 2026 landscape by itself.
The 2026 HFS compliance examination reported repeated weaknesses in cybersecurity programs and practices, inadequate IT general controls and inadequate data-protection controls.

The 2026 IDPH compliance examination reported repeated cybersecurity weaknesses, including missing or incomplete risk, data-classification, backup and vulnerability-management controls during the audit period; IDPH reported establishing a cybersecurity plan effective in 2026.

HFS disclosed phishing-related incidents in 2024 and 2025 affecting employee accounts and potentially exposing Medicaid or other personally identifiable information. These incidents are treated as observed security outcomes, not evidence that every Illinois health system shares the same risk.

LRN-5 is not assessed for Illinois v0.1. Public audit responses and collaboration forums demonstrate formal answerability and correction mechanisms, but they do not establish representative response times to documented external inquiries across the Illinois health-information environment.

sources.title: HealthChoice Illinois ADT
sources.publisher: Illinois Department of Healthcare and Family Services
sources.note: Current HFS page for the statewide Medicaid ADT exchange platform. HFS states that all managed care organizations are onboarded and that the majority of technically capable skilled nursing facilities contribute ADT data.

indicators.summary: Documents a statewide operational Medicaid exchange platform using real-time ADT notifications.
indicators.limitation: ADT exchange is narrower than full longitudinal clinical-record interoperability.

indicators.summary: Documents mandatory or broad participation across hospitals and multiple Medicaid provider classes.
indicators.limitation: The page does not provide a complete 2026 denominator-based participation rate for every provider category.

sources.replacement_reason: Public source and expected evidence independently rechecked on 24 September 2026.

sources.title: HealthChoice Illinois ADT FAQ
sources.publisher: Illinois Department of Healthcare and Family Services
sources.note: HFS describes mandatory participation rules, HL7 transmission requirements and no-cost connection/subscription for covered providers.

indicators.summary: Shows enforceable state Medicaid participation requirements and a defined operating model for ADT exchange.
indicators.limitation: The governance applies to the HFS ADT platform and does not constitute a single statewide governance layer for all health information.

indicators.summary: Documents required participation for hospitals and specified community, behavioral-health and long-term-care provider groups.
indicators.limitation: Requirements do not by themselves prove complete conformance or routine use at every site.

sources.replacement_reason: Public source and expected evidence independently rechecked on 24 September 2026.

sources.title: HFS HL7 ADT Data Quality Standards
sources.publisher: Illinois Department of Healthcare and Family Services
sources.note: HFS publishes data-quality requirements for HL7 ADT messages used by the statewide platform.

indicators.summary: Provides explicit technical and data-quality requirements for standardized ADT exchange.
indicators.limitation: The standard is message-specific and does not establish statewide FHIR or semantic interoperability for all clinical data.

sources.replacement_reason: Public source and expected evidence independently rechecked on 24 September 2026.

sources.title: Syndromic Surveillance
sources.note: IDPH states that it collects emergency-department syndromic data from all 185 acute-care hospitals in Illinois and that most facilities submit near-real-time data.

indicators.summary: Provides strong state-specific evidence of broad operational hospital data submission to public health.
indicators.limitation: Coverage concerns syndromic surveillance, not all clinical exchange use cases.

indicators.summary: Shows an operational statewide public-health data flow with rapid availability for surveillance.
indicators.limitation: The page is outcome-oriented and does not fully document every transport and semantic layer.

sources.replacement_reason: Public source and expected evidence independently rechecked on 24 September 2026.

sources.title: Illinois Electronic Visit Verification
sources.publisher: Illinois Department of Healthcare and Family Services
sources.note: Illinois uses a statewide EVV vendor/aggregator model and identifies a March 2, 2026 integration milestone for PCS and HHCS data from additional state provider groups.

indicators.summary: Documents a statewide aggregation architecture accepting data from multiple qualified EVV vendors.
indicators.limitation: EVV is a bounded administrative/operational dataset rather than a general clinical interoperability layer.

indicators.summary: Ongoing implementation milestones, town halls and technical guidance show iterative programme adjustment.
indicators.limitation: Programme iteration does not prove effective correction across the wider health-information environment.

sources.replacement_reason: Public source and expected evidence independently rechecked on 24 September 2026.

sources.title: IMPACT Login and identity proofing
sources.publisher: Illinois Department of Healthcare and Family Services
sources.note: HFS requires individual user accounts and identity proofing for access to IMPACT; provider enrollment also uses NPI-linked identity data.

indicators.summary: Documents individual identity proofing and non-shareable user identity for a major Illinois Medicaid provider system.
indicators.limitation: Provider-system identity proofing is not equivalent to a universal patient identity architecture.

sources.replacement_reason: Public source and expected evidence independently rechecked on 24 September 2026.

sources.title: HIE opt-out requirements — 740 ILCS 110/9.6
sources.note: Illinois law requires HIE participants to provide meaningful notice and a reasonable opportunity to opt out of further HIE disclosure, with revocation mechanisms.

indicators.summary: Establishes explicit state-level patient choice and disclosure requirements for HIE participation.
indicators.limitation: The law establishes rights and duties; it does not measure implementation quality at every HIE participant.

indicators.summary: Provides a durable legal governance layer for privacy and patient choice in health-information exchange.
indicators.limitation: Privacy governance does not replace operational interoperability governance.

sources.replacement_reason: Public link hidden after user-browser failure and independent fetch returned a server error on 24 September 2026. The official ILGA text remains documentary evidence pending public-link revalidation.

sources.title: Dissolution of the Health Information Exchange Office and Fund
sources.note: Current Illinois law documents the dissolution of the former Health Information Exchange Office and Fund following repeal of the Illinois Health Information Exchange and Technology Act.

indicators.summary: Confirms that Illinois no longer relies on the former dedicated state HIE authority/office governance model.
indicators.limitation: Dissolution does not imply absence of HIE; current exchange functions continue through HFS, IDPH, federal requirements and vendor networks.

sources.replacement_reason: Replaced the failing ILGA details URL with the current official ILCS Articles page independently verified on 24 September 2026.

sources.title: State Medicaid Health Information Technology Plan Update (2022)
sources.publisher: Illinois Department of Healthcare and Family Services
sources.note: The 2022 plan records that the state-run ILHIE model had been financially unsustainable and infrequently used, with limited regional HIE growth and increasing reliance on vendor-mediated exchange networks.

indicators.summary: Provides authoritative historical context for the shift from a state-run HIE toward distributed/vendor-mediated exchange.
indicators.limitation: The document is from 2021 and must not be treated as a complete description of the 2026 environment.

sources.replacement_reason: Document independently verified on 24 September 2026; the PDF itself is dated 30 March 2022, correcting the earlier 2021 label.

sources.title: HFS 2025 State Compliance Examination
sources.publisher: Illinois Office of the Auditor General
sources.note: The audit reported 13 current findings, 11 repeated findings, weaknesses in cybersecurity programs and practices, inadequate IT general controls, and inadequate data-protection controls. It also records prior recommendations implemented or not repeated.

indicators.summary: Independent audit evidence documents repeated cybersecurity, access-control and data-protection weaknesses at HFS.
indicators.limitation: The findings concern HFS systems and controls and do not establish the security posture of every Illinois healthcare organization.

indicators.summary: The audit provides a traceable correction mechanism with recommendations, management responses and follow-up of repeated findings.
indicators.limitation: Eleven of thirteen findings were repeated, indicating incomplete corrective follow-through in multiple areas.

indicators.summary: HFS formally accepts and responds to Auditor General recommendations.
indicators.limitation: Audit responses are not representative evidence of response times to external documented inquiries; LRN-5 remains not assessed.

sources.replacement_reason: Stable Auditor General audit index used as the public link; the full 2025 compliance report remains the documentary source.

sources.title: IDPH 2025 State Compliance Examination
sources.publisher: Illinois Office of the Auditor General
sources.note: The audit reported 40 current findings, 34 repeated findings, and repeated cybersecurity weaknesses. During the audit period IDPH lacked several documented cyber governance controls; IDPH reported a cybersecurity plan effective in 2026.

indicators.summary: Independent audit evidence documents repeated cybersecurity control weaknesses in a core Illinois public-health agency.
indicators.limitation: The Department reported remediation steps, including a 2026 cybersecurity plan; the audit period does not establish the post-remediation effectiveness of those changes.

indicators.summary: Formal audit follow-up records both repeated deficiencies and remediation actions.
indicators.limitation: A high proportion of repeated findings indicates that the correction cycle remains incomplete.

sources.replacement_reason: Stable Auditor General audit index used as the public link; the full 2025 compliance report remains the documentary source.

sources.title: HFS notice of phishing incident involving personally identifiable information
sources.publisher: Illinois Department of Healthcare and Family Services
sources.note: HFS disclosed a phishing incident compromising an employee account and documents, affecting 933 individuals, including 564 Illinois residents, with potentially exposed Medicaid and other personally identifiable information.

indicators.summary: Provides direct operational evidence of a realized security incident involving HFS-held sensitive information.
indicators.limitation: The event was limited in scale relative to the full Illinois health system and HFS documented containment, password reset and notification actions.

methodology.overall_rule: Rounded arithmetic mean of the six independent Illinois domain scores.
methodology.scope: State of Illinois health-information environment; federal rules are considered only where Illinois implementation is directly evidenced.
